correctness.rationale: The central-symmetry gap parameterization is exact and surjective for genuine cyclic hexagons. Direct shoelace and paired-edge calculations give the stated \(\Phi\) formula. Two-angle normalization gives a rational function with derivative \(v c(q-u)^2 B/D^2\), where \(D\) is the positive denominator. The polynomial factor satisfies \(B<0\) over \(0<u<1/\sqrt2\), \(\sqrt{1-u^2}<q\le1\), by the explicit \(u\le1/2\) and \(u>1/2\) bounds. Thus pairwise averaging strictly decreases \(\Phi\); iteration and the one-zero-angle boundary give the sharp range and equality classification. An embedded standard-library checker verified the polynomial identity and 4,275 finite diagnostic comparisons; those checks are not a substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The half-central-gap simplex is the complete natural moduli of cyclic centrally symmetric hexagons. Proving strict Schur-convexity of the geometrically motivated Levy ratio gives a global classification in the smallest nontrivial symmetric even cyclic-polygon case, uniquely identifies its regular lower extremizer and sharp nonattained upper boundary, and verifies a recognized unproved polygonal ratio conjecture on a multidimensional family. It is not a numerical table, arbitrary slice or routine substitution.
